seo_title: SC Backs NCLAT Power to Revisit Videocon Plan
title: Supreme Court Upholds NCLAT's Power to Send an Approved Resolution Plan Back to Creditors in Videocon Case
case_name: Twin Star Technologies Ltd.'s appeal against the NCLAT order reopening Videocon Industries Ltd.'s resolution plan
citation: Civil appeals against NCLAT's January 2022 order remitting the Videocon Industries resolution plan to the Committee of Creditors; Supreme Court judgment dated 16 November 2026
card_summary: The Supreme Court upheld an NCLAT order sending Twin Star Technologies' approved Rs 2,962 crore resolution plan for Videocon Industries back to the Committee of Creditors. Admitted claims ran to roughly Rs 65,000 crore, so the plan meant a haircut of more than 95 percent for creditors. The bench held that majority CoC approval cannot dispense with Section 30(2)(b)'s protection for dissenting creditors.
card_tip: Near-unanimous Committee of Creditors approval does not cure a plan that fails Section 30(2)(b)'s protection for dissenting financial creditors; NCLAT can still send an approved plan back for a fresh vote.
verification_notes: The 16 November 2026 date, the bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe, the Rs 2,962 crore plan value, the NCLAT's January 2022 remand order, and the haircut being described as 'more than 95 percent' are reported consistently across Bar and Bench, Business Standard and LawBeat (also TaxGuru and Gujarat Samachar, not cited to keep the source list to three). Sources differ on the precise admitted-claims figure (one states Rs 64,838.63 crore, others round to about Rs 65,000 crore), so the card states it as 'roughly Rs 65,000 crore' rather than the more precise but less-corroborated figure. The full judgment text was not independently opened; the account rests on these outlets' consistent reporting.
